newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end higher, CPI-linked bonds recover.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end higher, CPI-linked bonds recover.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed slightly higher on Wednesday, with CPI-linked bonds rising for the first time after four consecutive sessions, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.06 pct to 168.67
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct at 159.66
Volume was strong at 213 million shekels with all classes of bonds rising except dollar-linked bonds, which closed unchanged, traders said.

"Inflation-linked bonds recovered today, with most of the activity concentrated in long bonds. After four straight days of losses a technical correction had to come," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
"CPI-linked short bonds also did well, but trading activity was relatively low," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
Traders said unlinked bonds continued to post mild gains following a sharp rise since Sunday.
"Unlinked bonds gained almost one percent during the past week, and investors started taking profits," Kolka said.
"Unlinked bonds and Makams continue to be very attractive. Inflation is expected to decline while interest rates remain high," Rosenfeld added.

Traders attributed the quiet in the dollar-linked segment to the lack of movement in the dollar-shekel rate, which has been almost unchanged since Monday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2460 shekels against 3.2480 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
